findings.observation: The complete mace remains visible, but the butt and head approach roughly 5–7% from the left and right edges, crossing the required 8% safe margin.
Exactly one complete mace is present with no duplicate weapon, detached component, or extra gear.
The radial striking ribs around a compact head, straight haft, wrapped one-hand grip, and pommel read immediately as a flanged mace.

The collars, haft, grip wrap, and pommel are coherent, but the very large solid-looking spherical head and heavy encircling ribs are implausibly massive and poorly balanced for practical one-hand use.
Sunsteel dominates the head, ribs, haft, collars, and pommel as the sole rank-bearing material; the dark grip wrap remains subordinate and neutral.
Dense forged surfaces, rubbed silver edges, and restrained amber heat-light visible through fine fracture seams establish sunsteel through physical response beyond palette alone.
Amber emission is confined to fine fissures and small recessed motifs on the head and pommel; the mace does not become a full-object glow.
Premium realistic painterly rendering, honest wear, cold key light, restrained warm emission and rim, midnight-charcoal ground, and floor plane follow the accepted profile.

Most negative constraints pass, but the oversized spherical head violates no-oversized-silhouettes, and conspicuous sunburst medallions on head and pommel make ornament contribute materially to identity.
